Subject: Rapid close — econ gating & MAP milestones

Hi Samantha — great to meet yesterday. I promised to follow up with a focused Mutual Action Plan (MAP) slice we can use to unblock procurement and the pilot eval that needs to finish before Q2 close. Attached is a one‑page MAP (Aurelia_MAP_v3.pdf) and a lightweight token econ workbook.

Key asks from our side to accelerate pricing/PO approval:
- Confirm a target pilot cohort (number of end users per week) and typical average messages per session.
- Confirm whether message content is mostly short notifications (~50–150 tokens) or long summaries (~400–1,200 tokens).
- Agree to two gating checks we will run during the eval: cost ceiling (tokens/$) and quality pass rate on the provided eval set.

Proposed short MAP (timeline):
1) Week 0: Share pilot traffic profile + PO template (you)
2) Week 1: Redwood provides token‑per‑session econ and caching/batching plan (us)
3) Week 2: Pilot starts (Aurelia) — Redwood runs cost telemetry & recommends runtime knobs
4) Week 3: Eval result + procurement signoff decision

Practical econ notes (brief):
- We'll model tokens/$ at both raw and cached levels (prefix caching) and show sensitivity to batching (throughput vs latency).
- If 60% of tokens are stable prefixes, caching can reduce token spend by ~40% in our model; batching changes unit cost by pooling KV cache hits but may add 10–40ms p95 latency.

Can you confirm the pilot cohort estimate and whether procurement needs any additional compliance docs? I'll loop in our PM/engineering to produce an explicit tokens/$ scenario tailored to your cohort.

Thanks —Kimberly

All — attached is the token_econ_workbook_AH.xlsx export and a short one‑pager PDF (token_econ_summary_AH.pdf). Summary bullets below:
- Baseline (no caching, no batching): 150 users/week * 3 sessions * 250 tokens = ~33,750 tokens/week -> ~135k tokens/month. At our hosted price point that maps to: Best: $0.85k/mo, Likely: $1.2k/mo, Worst: $1.9k/mo (assumptions tab in workbook).
- Conservative caching scenario (30% prefix hit): token spend drops ~28% -> Likely case ~ $0.86k/mo. Optimistic caching (60% prefix hit): drop ~48% -> Likely case ~ $0.62k/mo.
- Batching (batch=16) lowers per‑token overheads but adds ~22ms p95; batch=4 is a good middle ground (~8ms p95). Recommended runtime: batch target=4, adaptive batching in bursts, prefix caching enabled with KV TTL 10m for pilot.
- Quantization: Rishi notes 4bit quant gives 1.6–2x token throughput improvement with ~12–18ms latency benefit on our test hardware; we recommend going with dynamic kernel selection rather than forcing quant for pilot to reduce risk.

Action items for procurement PO: include the itemized month‑1 estimate (we'll attach the one‑pager), a pilot term (30 days), and a demo access link for audit/SOC docs.

Priyom Das

Samantha / Procurement — attaching the finalized MAP slice and the econ one‑pager (token_econ_summary_AH.pdf). Agreed gating and timeline:
- Pilot cohort: 150 active users/week; target pilot start: Week of May 6
- Eval gates (to pass):
  • Cost gate: month‑1 projected run rate must be <= $1,200 with conservative caching (30% prefix hits)
  • Quality gate: pass rate >= 92% on the provided eval set (we'll run the eval and deliver a report at day 14)
  • Latency gate: p95 < 200ms for user‑visible requests (recommended batch target=4)
- Procurement deliverables: itemized month‑1 cost summary (attached), SOC2 attestation link, and PO template.

Next steps:
1) Aurelia to confirm pilot start date (we proposed May 6) and send PO draft to procurement.
2) Redwood to provision pilot keys and a telemetry dashboard; we will enable prefix caching + adaptive batching by default and share the telemetry link within 24 hours of provisioning.
3) At day 14 of pilot, Redwood will produce the tokens/$ report and the eval quality report; procurement can use the attached one‑pager for the PO attachment.

Happy to jump on a quick 20‑minute call if you want to walk procurement through the one‑pager.

Thanks —Kim
